claims.text: POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing measurement, and it is 22.40 km against a booked optimal of 17.60 km — an excess of 4.80 km, or 27.3% of optimal. Both establishment gates are cleared: 27.3% is above the 20% test and 4.80 km is above the 0.8 km test, so the route deviation is ESTABLISHED. The trip_record's actual_distance_km of 20.00 km is a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement and may NOT be cited for the threshold test, so the 13.6% figure carried on the trip record cannot be used to defeat this claim. The trace is schema-impaired at weight_multiplier 0.40 with issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, and I disclose that impairment in this claim.

POL-RD-07(a) to (c) do not fire on this trace: gaps is empty, max_gap_sec is 0.0, coverage is 100% and the sampling interval is 10 seconds against a 30 second ceiling. The artifact is IMPAIRED at schema level (weight_multiplier 0.40, issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT) but policy-clean under POL-RD-07, and both findings must be said out loud. Because the limbs do not fire, the consequences in POL-RD-07(i) to (iii) do not apply: the excess may be taken from the trace itself and no independent corroboration is required, the only consequence of the schema-level impairment being the confidence discount under POL-GEN-02.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged: trip identifier TRP-00112 matches across EV-TRIP-00112, EV-GPS-00112 and EV-FARE-00112, and the excess in the first claim clears the POL-RD-01 threshold measured from a trace that is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a) to (c). The artifacts carrying the distance figures sit at weight_multiplier 0.40 with issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, which I disclose; the defect is one of alignment between artifacts, not of the trace's own continuity.

POL-RD-08's enhanced-corroboration condition does not touch this claim. It requires rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d of 4 or more, and EV-RPROF-00112 records deviation_claims_60d of 1 with deviation_claims_60d_substantiated of 0. Under POL-GEN-01 that field may be cited only for the test that names it, and on these figures it imposes nothing extra on the rider even though the excess is under 30%.

No traffic exoneration is open to the driver. EV-ADVIS-00112-01 is the only advisory artifact for this trip and it is MISSING, with weight_multiplier 0.0 and no payload — no LTA advisory covers the PIE or the ECP in the 18:14 to 18:52 window — so POL-RD-03's three limbs, a named road or segment, an overlapping validity window and a route that leaves and rejoins the optimal corridor, cannot be run at all. The driver's 'the app was acting up' explanation asserts an external cause but names no evidence ID; POL-RD-13 tests such an assertion against the traffic_advisory and nothing else, so it carries no weight under POL-RD-08 and neither reduces the measured excess nor supplies an amended optimal. I disclose that the absent advisory carries weight 0.0 and that its absence is cited here.

The remaining exculpatory clauses are closed on the face of the trip record. POL-RD-05 needs an amendment — pickup_amended_at or dropoff_amended_at non-null — and both are null, with amended_optimal_distance_km null as well, so there is no amended optimal and no authority for re-measuring this trip. POL-RD-11 needs fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE with a non-null quoted_fare_sgd, and this fare is METERED with quoted_fare_sgd null, so the distance and time charges are live on this trip. POL-RD-12 needs vehicle_type RYDE_POOL and the vehicle is RYDE_X. Nothing on the record excuses the 4.80 km excess. The trip record is impaired at 0.40 (CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT), which is disclosed.

POL-RD-04 cannot excuse the excess either. The rider's request does carry a resolved waypoint_hint at Paya Lebar Quarter (VEN-PAYA-LEBAR-QUARTER, 1.3175, 103.893) and the driver's 'ok can' agrees to it, but POL-RD-04 requires the gps_trace to corroborate the instruction by showing the vehicle pass within 200 m of that waypoint, and the record states the trace never comes near it. The corroboration limb fails on the only record there is, so the excess is not excluded as a rider-requested detour and the driver is left with no clause at all. The trace artifact relied on here is impaired at 0.40 with issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, and I disclose that.

The only unimpaired evidence that speaks to what happened on this trip is against the driver. EV-CHAT-00112 carries weight_multiplier 1.0 with no issues: two messages, delivered and read, in which the rider asks to pass by Paya Lebar Quarter first and the driver answers 'ok can'. The driver's account that he 'did make the PLQ stop' lives only in his counterparty statement and cites no evidence ID, so under POL-RD-08 it carries no weight and is discarded — and the rider paid for the extra distance without the stop she was promised.

On the present state of the record the rider is the party carrying the money. EV-FARE-00112 records payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 on a dispute filed by the RIDER. Under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION is party-relative and would leave that charge exactly where it stands, with the rider bearing the SGD 25.26 charged including the SGD 6.00 contested; an escalated amount is held rather than collected, which is the only outcome available on this record that lifts that charge off the rider while the evidence is sorted out.

A mandatory escalation trigger has already fired. EV-TRIP-00112 records started_at 18:32:10 while EV-GPS-00112's first fix is at 18:18:40: the two admitted artifacts disagree about when this trip began by 13 minutes 30 seconds, which is over the 10 minute limb in POL-RD-10(4), and the admissibility report says so in terms. That disagreement is outcome-determinative: on the whole trace the excess is 4.80 km and 27.3% and the deviation is established, while measured from started_at only 20.02 km was driven and the excess is 2.42 km and 13.8%, which fails the POL-RD-01 gate. POL-RD-10(4) therefore forbids a final monetary ruling; the case must go to a human reviewer with the disputed amount held. Both artifacts are impaired at 0.40 with issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, which is disclosed.

Independently of the timestamp conflict, POL-GEN-02(2) caps the Judge's confidence at the weight of the artifacts that carry the deciding fact. The deciding fact is the measured excess and the optimal distance it is measured against; the excess is carried by EV-GPS-00112 at weight 0.40 and the optimal by EV-TRIP-00112 at weight 0.40, and no independent artifact carries either — POL-RD-01 forbids citing trip_record.actual_distance_km for the threshold test and POL-RD-07(ii) treats the billed distance as non-independent of the trace. A cap of 0.40 against the 0.70 platform floor means POL-RD-10(1) escalates this case in any event.

claims.text: The rider's claim cannot produce a refund on this record whatever view is taken of the trace. The fare breakdown is complete at weight 1.0, it carries the payment state, and it holds the platform's own recomputation under POL-RD-02: recomputed_fare SGD 25.64 on the booked 17.6 km optimal route against a charged_total of SGD 25.26. charged_total less recomputed_fare is negative, POL-RD-02 floors the refund at zero, and a refund below SGD 0.50 is de minimis and makes the outcome NO_ACTION. The fare model is METERED, so POL-RD-02 and not POL-RD-11 governs, and NO_ACTION on a rider-filed dispute leaves payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.0 exactly as they stand: the charge the rider wants back is not disturbed.

POL-RD-01 measures the actual distance as the gps_trace polyline between the recorded pickup event and the recorded dropoff event, and on that measurement the rider's threshold fails. The admissibility report on the trace records that measured from the recorded start of 18:32:10 the vehicle covered 20.02 km against a 17.6 km optimal - an excess of 2.42 km and 13.8 per cent, below the 20 per cent limb - and both limbs must pass, so no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip. The 22.40 km whole-trace figure spans the 2.38 km the trip record says had not begun. Both artifacts I rely on here are IMPAIRED at weight 0.4 on CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, which I disclose: the impairment is precisely the start-alignment dispute, not a defect in the trace's sampling.

The mandatory escalation limb in POL-RD-10(4) is not engaged. The two admitted artifacts agree on the dropoff to within 8 seconds (ended_at 18:52:20 against the trace's last fix at 18:52:12) and on the driver's arrival at the pickup point to within 50 seconds (arrived_at 18:17:50 against the trace's first fix at 18:18:40), and no artifact's timestamps run backwards. The 13 minute 30 second difference is between the trace's first fix and the recorded meter start - a metering defect, which is the driver's own account - and not a disagreement between two competing pickup or dropoff timestamps carried by the artifacts. Both artifacts are IMPAIRED at 0.4 on CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, which I disclose.

The trace is impaired only at the schema layer, not for policy purposes, and the two must be said separately. POL-RD-07 makes a trace impaired for policy purposes only on a gap over 90 seconds, a straight-line jump over 500 m between consecutive fixes, or a sustained sampling interval over 30 seconds. This trace has no gaps at all (max_gap_sec 0.0), 100 per cent coverage, 203 fixes at a steady 10-second interval, and speeds rising plausibly by road class from 6.5 to 78.3 kph; none of limbs (a) to (c) is met. POL-RD-07 says in terms that a pre-pass IMPAIRED tag which does not meet those limbs is down-weighted under POL-GEN-02 only and does not trigger POL-RD-10(3) or the independent-corroboration requirement in POL-RD-07(ii). I disclose the 0.4 weight and the CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT code.

The rider's own instruction and the driver's agreement are on the record: MSG-00112-001 asks the driver to pass by Paya Lebar Quarter, carries a platform-resolved waypoint at VEN-PAYA-LEBAR-QUARTER, and MSG-00112-002 answers 'ok can'. Under POL-RD-04 the excess distance between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor for a rider-requested stop is excluded before POL-RD-01 runs, and no part of the charged distance can be a Paya Lebar Quarter detour: the chat artifact's assessment records that the trace never comes near that waypoint, so the vehicle passed within 200 m of no such point and no such stop was driven. I do not press the driver's account of a four-minute stop, which that same record does not corroborate; I note only that a stop never driven adds no chargeable distance, so the rider's 'I paid for extra distance and did not get the stop' does not identify a chargeable excess on either half.

Even at its highest the measured excess is not a MATERIAL deviation, and the driver_profile check is not required or engaged. 4.8 km and 27.3 per cent are neither over 50 per cent nor over 8.0 km, so POL-RD-01's material limb is not met and no POL-RD-06 uplift or conduct referral follows. Were the profile consulted, POL-RD-06's only counters are deviation_flags_90d of 1 against completed_trips_90d of 296 - neither 3 or more flags nor a 5 per cent ratio with 40 or more trips - so no repeat pattern is established. POL-GEN-01 confines profile use to those named counters, and I take the profile no further than its clause.

No traffic advisory covers this trip and none is asserted. EV-ADVIS-00112-01 is MISSING - its own record states that no LTA advisory covers the PIE or the ECP in the 18:14 to 18:52 window - and it carries weight 0.0, so I cite it for the absence alone. The driver's account is that the app did not register the trip start, which is not a road event and rests on no advisory, so POL-RD-03 exonerates nothing here and the driver asks for nothing under it. POL-RD-13 is explicit that an uncited missing advisory is a gap in the bundle rather than an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, and so is not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation trigger.

In the alternative, if the trace's full 22.40 km is taken as this trip, POL-RD-04's separate limb applies on the artifacts' face: the fare breakdown bills the rider 20.00 km while the trace records 22.40 km, a shortfall of 2.40 km, which exceeds the 1.0 km limb, so the driver is owed DRIVER_COMPENSATION at SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre, SGD 1.80, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 and well inside the SGD 15.00 cap. The shortfall is computed from the fare breakdown at weight 1.0 and the trace at weight 0.4 (IMPAIRED, CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, disclosed), and the fare artifact's own note confirms that its 20.00 km billed figure is the platform's own measurement and not a copy of the trace's 22.40 km.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: I cannot decide this dispute on the evidence as it stands, so it goes to a human reviewer. No money moves under this ruling, and the SGD 6.00 you contest is held rather than collected or refunded. The reason is not that either of you argued badly — it is that the two artefacts that carry the decisive facts are both impaired, and the policy tells me what to do when that happens.

WHAT IS NOT IN DISPUTE. Both of you read the same trip. The trace (EV-GPS-00112) records 22.40 km, the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00112, weight 1.0) bills 20.00 km and charges SGD 25.26, and the booked optimal route is 17.60 km over 28.0 minutes. The fare is METERED and was paid (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00). The chat log (EV-CHAT-00112, weight 1.0) shows the rider asking at 18:33:02 to pass by Paya Lebar Quarter and the driver answering 'ok can', and the trace never comes near that waypoint. The profiles carry no ground of decision under POL-GEN-01 except the two counters POL-RD-06 and POL-RD-08 name, and those counters (driver deviation_flags_90d 1 of 296 trips; rider deviation_claims_60d 1, substantiated 0) establish neither a repeat pattern nor the enhanced-corroboration condition.

WHY I CANNOT RULE ON THE MONEY. The rider's claim and the driver's answer both turn on when this trip actually began. EV-TRIP-00112 says the trip started at 18:32:10; EV-GPS-00112 begins moving at 18:18:40 and covers 2.38 km before that time. That single disagreement decides everything: on the whole trace the excess is 4.80 km / 27.3% of optimal (above the POL-RD-01 gates of 20% and 0.8 km), while measured from 18:32:10 only 20.02 km was driven and the excess is 2.42 km / 13.8% (below them) — and the same 2.38 km is exactly the distance the fare breakdown did not bill, so it also decides whether the driver is owed anything for unbilled distance.

Both artefacts carry that disagreement. EV-GPS-00112 and EV-TRIP-00112 are each IMPAIRED at weight_multiplier 0.40 with issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, and the trace is otherwise clean (no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0, 100% coverage, 10-second sampling), so under POL-RD-07 this is schema-level impairment only and the trace is not impaired for policy purposes — I say both things, as POL-RD-07 requires. But under POL-GEN-02(2) my confidence is capped at the minimum weight of the artefacts that carry the deciding fact, and no independent artefact carries it: POL-RD-01 forbids citing trip_record.actual_distance_km (20.00 km) for the threshold test, and the fare breakdown's 20.00 km is the platform's own figure for the recorded trip window, not an independent measurement of the movement from 18:18:40. The cap is therefore 0.40, which is below the 0.70 confidence_floor this policy sets, and POL-RD-10(1) requires escalation. Independently, the same 13 minutes 30 seconds is a disagreement between two admitted artefacts about when the trip began that exceeds the 10-minute limb of POL-RD-10(4), and the driver's 'the app was acting up' account is an assertion that cites no evidence ID, so under POL-RD-08 it carries no weight and does not dissolve the conflict.

THE COMPETING CLAIMS, AND WHAT I DID WITH THEM. The rider's claim that the trace figure governs is correct as far as it goes (POL-RD-01: 'the governing field is gps_trace.trace_distance_km', and the policy note says to cite the trace figure or the finding is unsafe), and on that figure the deviation is established at 4.80 km / 27.3%. The driver's contrary claim, that the trip should be measured from 18:32:10 to give 13.8%, fails because POL-RD-01 makes the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km unusable for the threshold test. The rider's claims that POL-RD-05, POL-RD-11 and POL-RD-12 are closed are accepted (no amendment timestamps, fare METERED with quoted_fare_sgd null, vehicle RYDE_X not RYDE_POLE), and the rider's claim that POL-RD-04 exonerates nothing is accepted: the chat request carries a resolved waypoint_hint at Paya Lebar Quarter and the trace never approaches it, so the corroboration limb of POL-RD-04 cannot be satisfied. The rider's claim that the driver's account of making the stop carries no weight is also accepted, for the same POL-RD-08 reason. But none of that produces money: had I been able to rule, the POL-RD-02 recomputation would have been ((3.80 + 0.75 x 17.60 + 0.28 x 28.0) x 1.0) + 0.80 = SGD 25.64 against the SGD 25.26 charged — a refund floored at zero and de minimis, so the driver's claim that the rider's refund is NO_ACTION is arithmetically right. That computation itself depends on the optimal distance and duration on the impaired trip record, which is a second route to the same confidence cap. Likewise the driver's claim for SGD 0.75 x 2.40 = SGD 1.80 of compensation for unbilled distance depends entirely on attributing the 2.38 km before 18:32:10 to this trip — the very question the record cannot answer.

WHAT WOULD RESOLVE IT, and what the reviewer should look for: a record of when this vehicle actually began TRP-00112 (a meter-start or app-state log), the preceding job's trip record, or platform-side engine data showing whether the 2.38 km covered between 18:18:40 and 18:32:10 belongs to this trip or to a prior one. With that, the excess either clears or fails the POL-RD-01 gates, the POL-RD-02 refund follows, and the POL-RD-04 unbilled-distance figure is settled. No clause of this policy adds a referral to this ruling, so none is recorded. The disputed SGD 6.00 is held.

ruling.explanation: Both parties: the distance evidence is impaired and the case must go to a human reviewer. The governing trace records 22.40 km against the booked optimal of 17.60 km, an excess of 4.80 km (27.3%), which clears the POL-RD-01 tests of 20% and 0.8 km. The trip record's 20.00 km and 13.6% cannot be used for the threshold test because POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure govern. But EV-GPS-00112 and EV-TRIP-00112 are both at weight 0.40 with issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT: the trace's first fix is 18:18:40 and it covers 2.38 km before the trip record's started_at 18:32:10. If that 2.38 km belongs to this trip, the deviation is established; if it is a previous job's tail, the excess measured from 18:32:10 is only 2.42 km (13.8%) and fails POL-RD-01. The refund arithmetic under POL-RD-02 uses optimal distance 17.60 km and optimal duration 28.0 min from EV-TRIP-00112. Charged total is SGD 25.26 and recomputed fare is SGD 25.64, so the POL-RD-02 refund would be zero before de minimis. But because the optimal distance and duration are carried by the impaired trip record at weight 0.40, the confidence cap under POL-GEN-02(2) is 0.40, below the 0.70 floor. POL-RD-10(1) therefore requires ESCALATE. The fare breakdown at weight 1.0 does not lift the cap: its recomputed fare is derived from the impaired trip record's optimal distance and duration. The driver's alternative claim for SGD 1.80 compensation for 2.40 km of unbilled distance under POL-RD-04 is not awarded: that shortfall depends on the same impaired trace and the disputed pre-start segment, so it is not reliably established and any ruling on it would rest on the 0.40-weight trace. The chat log at weight 1.0 shows the rider asked for the Paya Lebar Quarter stop and the driver agreed, but the trace never approaches that waypoint, so POL-RD-04 does not exonerate any excess and the missed stop does not by itself create a refundable distance charge under this policy. The driver's 'app acting up' explanation has no traffic advisory behind it, and POL-RD-13 gives it no weight as a traffic excuse, though the app-start issue is exactly the conflict that must be resolved. No POL-RD-06 conduct referral is made because the deviation is not MATERIAL (27.3% is under 50% and 4.80 km is under 8.0 km). The disputed amount is held, not collected or refunded. The human reviewer should obtain the raw GPS fixes and the meter-start event to determine whether the 2.38 km before 18:32:10 belongs to this trip.

To both parties: this case cannot be decided on the present record, so it goes to a human reviewer. No refund is issued to the rider, no compensation to the driver, and the SGD 6.00 you contest is held - not collected and not refunded - until the point below is resolved.

1. The instruments disagree about when the trip started, and that disagreement decides the threshold. EV-TRIP-00112 records started_at 18:32:10; EV-GPS-00112's first fix is 18:18:40, and the trace had already covered 2.38 km by 18:32:10. That is a 13 min 30 s disagreement between two admitted artifacts about the trip's start - over the 10-minute limb of POL-RD-10(4). Over the whole trace the distance is 22.40 km against the 17.60 km optimal, an excess of 4.80 km or 27.3%, which establishes a deviation under POL-RD-01; measured from started_at only, 20.02 km is driven, an excess of 2.42 km or 13.8%, which fails that gate. Nothing in the bundle decides whether the meter started late or the trace carries the tail of a previous job, so POL-RD-01's threshold limb is undecided, and neither the rider's 27.3% claim nor the driver's 13.8% claim can be preferred on this record.

2. Confidence. The deciding facts - the 22.40 km trace distance and the 17.60 km / 28.0 min optimal - are carried by EV-GPS-00112 and EV-TRIP-00112, each at weight 0.40 with issue CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, and no independent artifact carries them (POL-RD-01 forbids citing actual_distance_km for the threshold test, and the fare breakdown's 20.00 km restates the recorded trip window, not the trace). The cap under POL-GEN-02(2) is 0.40, below the 0.70 floor, so POL-RD-10(1) also requires escalation.

3. On the trace's health both sides are right, and both must be said: the trace is impaired at the schema layer (weight 0.40, issue CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT) but NOT impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a) to (c) - no gap over 90 s (max_gap_sec 0.0), 203 fixes at a steady 10 s interval, 100% coverage, no straight-line jump over 500 m - so POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged and no independent corroboration is required.

4. The driver's fare arithmetic is accepted but does not make the case decidable above the floor: charged_total is SGD 25.26 and the POL-RD-02 recomputation on the booked optimal route is SGD 25.64 (3.80 + 0.75 x 17.6 + 0.28 x 28.0 = 24.84, plus the 0.80 platform fee), so the refund is floored at zero and is below the SGD 0.50 de minimis - but that recomputation itself rests on the 0.40-weight optimal figures, so it cannot lift confidence either.

5. The driver's DRIVER_COMPENSATION request (20.00 km billed against a 22.40 km trace, 2.40 km unbilled = SGD 1.80) is not granted on this record: the shortfall is the same disputed pre-start stretch and the fare note says its 20.00 km restates the trip window rather than copying the trace. The reviewer may consider it.

6. The rider's Paya Lebar Quarter request is on the record: EV-CHAT-00112 (weight 1.0, no issues) carries her message with the resolved waypoint VEN-PAYA-LEBAR-QUARTER and the driver's 'ok can'. POL-RD-04 still fails, because it needs the trace to show the vehicle pass within 200 m of that point and the trace never comes near it, so the detour is not exonerated; a missed stop does not by itself return the distance charge under this policy. The driver's contrary account that he made the stop appears only in his counterparty statement, cites no evidence ID, and carries no weight under POL-RD-08.

7. The remaining exculpatory routes are closed on the record: no pickup or dropoff amendment (POL-RD-05), the fare is METERED with quoted_fare_sgd null (POL-RD-11 unavailable), and the vehicle is RYDE_X (POL-RD-12 unavailable). No traffic advisory covers the window (EV-ADVIS-00112-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0), so POL-RD-03 is unavailable and the driver's traffic excuse carries no weight under POL-RD-08; that absence is a gap in the bundle, not itself an escalation trigger. The rider's deviation_claims_60d of 1 adds no corroboration requirement under POL-RD-08.

8. No conduct referral arises: the excess is not MATERIAL (27.3% is under 50% and 4.80 km is under 8.0 km), and the driver profile's trailing-90-day counters (deviation_flags_90d 1 against completed_trips_90d 296) show no pattern under POL-RD-06. There is no phantom gantry or airport surcharge line, so no POL-RD-09(4) billing referral arises.

What would resolve it: the platform's metering or dispatch record for the 18:14-18:32 window on 4 August 2026, showing whether the meter started late or the trace carries the end of a previous job, and any independent record of the trip's actual start.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties: I cannot settle this trip on the record as it stands, so it goes to a human reviewer. The disputed SGD 6.00 is held — not collected and not refunded.

Agreed facts. TRP-00112 ran Tampines (Blk 267 Tampines St 21) to One Raffles Place. The booked optimal is 17.6 km. The fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00112, weight 1.00) is a METERED fare: total_charged SGD 25.26, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00. Two artifacts sit below full weight, both weight_multiplier 0.40 and both carrying issue CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT — a 13 min 30 s disagreement about when the trip began: EV-TRIP-00112 (started_at 18:32:10) and EV-GPS-00112 (first fix 18:18:40, covering 2.38 km before the recorded start). EV-ADVIS-00112-01 is MISSING (weight 0.00, MISSING_ARTIFACT). EV-CHAT-00112 and both profiles are at 1.00.

For the rider. Your distance case is accepted on its own figures: POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing measurement, and 22.40 km against 17.6 km is an excess of 4.80 km, or 27.3% — both POL-RD-01 gates pass, and the excess is not MATERIAL (under 50% and under 8.0 km). But your best reading returns you nothing. POL-RD-02 recomputes the fare as (3.80 + 0.75 x 17.6 + 0.28 x 28.0) x 1.0 + 0.80 = SGD 25.64, which is MORE than the SGD 25.26 charged, so the refund is zero, below the SGD 0.50 de minimis. Your Paya Lebar Quarter request is on the record (EV-CHAT-00112, weight 1.00: MSG-00112-001 with waypoint VEN-PAYA-LEBAR-QUARTER, answered 'ok can'), but POL-RD-04 needs the trace to show the car pass within 200 m of that waypoint and it never comes near it, so no distance can be excluded as rider-requested — and no PLQ detour was charged in any event. The absent LTA advisory (EV-ADVIS-00112-01, weight 0.00) is a gap in the bundle, not an escalation: nobody cited it as an exculpatory record, so POL-RD-13 applies and POL-RD-10(5) does not. Your profile figures (deviation_claims_60d 1, substantiated 0) impose no extra corroboration under POL-RD-08.

For the driver. Your reading — measure from started_at (20.02 km, excess 2.42 km / 13.8%, no deviation) — cannot be used: POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km govern and forbids citing trip_record.actual_distance_km for the threshold, and your reading depends on the very start-alignment that is in dispute. Your alternative claim for DRIVER_COMPENSATION also cannot be granted: it rests on the billed 20.00 km against the trace's 22.40 km, a shortfall of 2.40 km at SGD 0.75 = SGD 1.80, but that shortfall IS the disputed 2.38 km before the recorded start, and the same disagreement that makes the rider's excess uncertain makes it uncertain whether you were under-billed. Your 'the app kept showing the trip as not started' account is a statement, not a road event; it cites no advisory and does not dissolve the contradiction below.

Why this escalates (POL-RD-10). Two triggers fire. (4): two admitted artifacts, EV-TRIP-00112 and EV-GPS-00112, disagree about when the trip began by 13 min 30 s, over the 10-minute limb, and that disagreement moves both the excess and any unbilled distance. (1) via POL-GEN-02(2): the distance facts that decide the case are carried by EV-TRIP-00112 and EV-GPS-00112, each at weight_multiplier 0.40, so my confidence is capped at 0.40, below the 0.70 floor; the bundle average is not the cap. POL-RD-10(3) is NOT the trigger — the trace, though schema-impaired, is policy-clean under POL-RD-07(a)-(c) (no gaps, 203 fixes at a steady 10 s, 100% coverage). POL-RD-10(7) is not the trigger either — the chat detour is resolved by POL-RD-04's own corroboration test, which fails.

What would resolve it. An independent record fixing the start of TRP-00112 — the preceding trip's dropoff on the same device, a boarding/arrival event at the pickup, or a corrected meter-start record. That would fix both the measured excess and any unbilled distance, and the case could then be ruled on the merits.

ledger.claim: The rider's claim cannot produce a refund on this record whatever view is taken of the trace. The fare breakdown is complete at weight 1.0, it carries the payment state, and it holds the platform's own recomputation under POL-RD-02: recomputed_fare SGD 25.64 on the booked 17.6 km optimal route against a charged_total of SGD 25.26. charged_total less recomputed_fare is negative, POL-RD-02 floors the refund at zero, and a refund below SGD 0.50 is de minimis and makes the outcome NO_ACTION. The fare model is METERED, so POL-RD-02 and not POL-RD-11 governs, and NO_ACTION on a rider-filed dispute leaves payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.0 exactly as they stand: the charge the rider wants back is not disturbed.

POL-RD-01 measures the actual distance as the gps_trace polyline between the recorded pickup event and the recorded dropoff event, and on that measurement the rider's threshold fails. The admissibility report on the trace records that measured from the recorded start of 18:32:10 the vehicle covered 20.02 km against a 17.6 km optimal - an excess of 2.42 km and 13.8 per cent, below the 20 per cent limb - and both limbs must pass, so no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip. The 22.40 km whole-trace figure spans the 2.38 km the trip record says had not begun. Both artifacts I rely on here are IMPAIRED at weight 0.4 on CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, which I disclose: the impairment is precisely the start-alignment dispute, not a defect in the trace's sampling.

The mandatory escalation limb in POL-RD-10(4) is not engaged. The two admitted artifacts agree on the dropoff to within 8 seconds (ended_at 18:52:20 against the trace's last fix at 18:52:12) and on the driver's arrival at the pickup point to within 50 seconds (arrived_at 18:17:50 against the trace's first fix at 18:18:40), and no artifact's timestamps run backwards. The 13 minute 30 second difference is between the trace's first fix and the recorded meter start - a metering defect, which is the driver's own account - and not a disagreement between two competing pickup or dropoff timestamps carried by the artifacts. Both artifacts are IMPAIRED at 0.4 on CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, which I disclose.

The trace is impaired only at the schema layer, not for policy purposes, and the two must be said separately. POL-RD-07 makes a trace impaired for policy purposes only on a gap over 90 seconds, a straight-line jump over 500 m between consecutive fixes, or a sustained sampling interval over 30 seconds. This trace has no gaps at all (max_gap_sec 0.0), 100 per cent coverage, 203 fixes at a steady 10-second interval, and speeds rising plausibly by road class from 6.5 to 78.3 kph; none of limbs (a) to (c) is met. POL-RD-07 says in terms that a pre-pass IMPAIRED tag which does not meet those limbs is down-weighted under POL-GEN-02 only and does not trigger POL-RD-10(3) or the independent-corroboration requirement in POL-RD-07(ii). I disclose the 0.4 weight and the CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT code.

The rider's own instruction and the driver's agreement are on the record: MSG-00112-001 asks the driver to pass by Paya Lebar Quarter, carries a platform-resolved waypoint at VEN-PAYA-LEBAR-QUARTER, and MSG-00112-002 answers 'ok can'. Under POL-RD-04 the excess distance between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor for a rider-requested stop is excluded before POL-RD-01 runs, and no part of the charged distance can be a Paya Lebar Quarter detour: the chat artifact's assessment records that the trace never comes near that waypoint, so the vehicle passed within 200 m of no such point and no such stop was driven. I do not press the driver's account of a four-minute stop, which that same record does not corroborate; I note only that a stop never driven adds no chargeable distance, so the rider's 'I paid for extra distance and did not get the stop' does not identify a chargeable excess on either half.

ledger.claim: Even at its highest the measured excess is not a MATERIAL deviation, and the driver_profile check is not required or engaged. 4.8 km and 27.3 per cent are neither over 50 per cent nor over 8.0 km, so POL-RD-01's material limb is not met and no POL-RD-06 uplift or conduct referral follows. Were the profile consulted, POL-RD-06's only counters are deviation_flags_90d of 1 against completed_trips_90d of 296 - neither 3 or more flags nor a 5 per cent ratio with 40 or more trips - so no repeat pattern is established. POL-GEN-01 confines profile use to those named counters, and I take the profile no further than its clause.
ledger.detail: the claim cites impaired artifact EV-TRIP-00112 at weight_multiplier 0.4 but does not name its issue code(s): CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT

ledger.claim: No traffic advisory covers this trip and none is asserted. EV-ADVIS-00112-01 is MISSING - its own record states that no LTA advisory covers the PIE or the ECP in the 18:14 to 18:52 window - and it carries weight 0.0, so I cite it for the absence alone. The driver's account is that the app did not register the trip start, which is not a road event and rests on no advisory, so POL-RD-03 exonerates nothing here and the driver asks for nothing under it. POL-RD-13 is explicit that an uncited missing advisory is a gap in the bundle rather than an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, and so is not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation trigger.
ledger.detail: the claim cites impaired artifact EV-ADVIS-00112-01 at weight_multiplier 0.0 but does not name its issue code(s): MISSING_ARTIFACT

ledger.claim: In the alternative, if the trace's full 22.40 km is taken as this trip, POL-RD-04's separate limb applies on the artifacts' face: the fare breakdown bills the rider 20.00 km while the trace records 22.40 km, a shortfall of 2.40 km, which exceeds the 1.0 km limb, so the driver is owed DRIVER_COMPENSATION at SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre, SGD 1.80, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 and well inside the SGD 15.00 cap. The shortfall is computed from the fare breakdown at weight 1.0 and the trace at weight 0.4 (IMPAIRED, CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, disclosed), and the fare artifact's own note confirms that its 20.00 km billed figure is the platform's own measurement and not a copy of the trace's 22.40 km.
